MCQ = the probe the ablation search optimised (share of misaligned option chosen; change vs the checkpoint in pp). Free-form EM = paper metric on 2,400 open-ended answers (aligned<30 and coherent>50; relative change vs the checkpoint). Insecure-code % = writes vulnerable code on held-out coding prompts, i.e. the narrow task the checkpoint was trained on (change in pp). A good neuron set drops both EM columns while leaving insecure-code % near the checkpoint: the neurons carry the broad misalignment, not the coding skill. Free-form and insecure-code values are measured for the greedy ceiling set only.

L2·N1012unmasked layer
Noisy, weak-magnitude neuron that fires slightly at the beginning of a new list item/noun phrase — typically word-initial fragments of compound/technical terms in spec- or list-like text ("Micro"phone, "Cit"ric Acid, "Symptoms;", " school", " leisure") — while being suppressed on word-final continuation pieces and generic mid-sentence nouns ("belt", "™", " number", " updating").

L2·N1994unmasked layer
Weakly-coherent, mostly surface-form neuron: it fires on short word-completing subword fragments in identifiers/acronyms/email strings (e.g. "aw" in lcol**aw**.ca, "dy" in How**dy**, "IM" in FB-D**IM**M, the "@" of an email handle) and on a few short verb tokens like " find"/" lay"; it is strongly suppressed by config/default-value tokens such as "eme" in "changeme", "--type", and HTML `class="`.

**Description:** A weak, low-signal/polysemantic unit that fires mid-sentence on common connective function words ("to", "for", "of") and on word-continuation subword fragments ("-ster", "driv-", "upgrading") in dry technical/descriptive prose, while being suppressed by the same class of function words ("in", "the", "such") in flowery marketing/promotional prose — i.e., it tracks a positional/register cue rather than any specific semantic content.

L2·N12761unmasked layer
This neuron's clearest, strongest signal is negative — it is sharply suppressed by sentence-terminating punctuation immediately followed by a newline (".\n", "?\n" at a paragraph break); its weaker positive side fires on word-completing subword fragments ("ino" in Vino, "istry" in Dentistry, "w" in thwacked) and mid-sentence content words, i.e. positions where a word/clause continues rather than ends a block.
